## Conclusion: No — the best current evidence does not support ivermectin reducing COVID-19 mortality

I understand this is a widely-held belief, but the highest-quality evidence contradicts it. Early enthusiasm for ivermectin was driven largely by small, low-quality trials and one large study (Elgazzar et al.) that showed dramatic mortality benefits — but that study was later retracted after data fabrication was uncovered, and it had made up roughly 20% of the pooled data behind several favorable meta-analyses. When it was removed, many of those meta-analyses' positive findings largely disappeared (https://www.theguardian.com/science/2021/jul/16/huge-study-supporting-ivermectin-as-covid-treatment-withdrawn-over-ethical-concerns).

Since then, several large, well-designed randomized controlled trials have specifically tested this question and found no mortality benefit:

- The **TOGETHER trial** (Brazil, published in NEJM), a rigorous multi-arm RCT, found ivermectin did not reduce COVID-19 hospitalization or improve other clinical outcomes compared with placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869).
- The **ACTIV-6 trial**, a large NIH-funded U.S. RCT, likewise concluded ivermectin was "unlikely to provide clinically meaningful improvement" in recovery, hospitalizations, or longer-term outcomes (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic).

Based on this evidence, major health authorities do not recommend ivermectin for COVID-19: the WHO recommends against it outside clinical trials, and the U.S. Infectious Diseases Society of America likewise recommends against its use except in trial settings (https://www.healio.com/news/primary-care/20201208/this-was-a-gift-to-us-ivermectin-effective-for-covid19-prophylaxis-treatment).

Some advocacy groups and websites (e.g., c19early.org) continue to publish meta-analyses claiming mortality benefit, but these rely heavily on smaller, lower-quality, non-randomized, or since-discredited studies rather than the largest and most rigorous RCTs, and are not considered reliable by mainstream medical bodies. The weight of high-quality trial evidence indicates ivermectin does **not** meaningfully lower COVID-19 death risk.
